What If the Tunguska Blast Happened Over a City?
It exploded in mid-air, leaving no crater.
The blast came 5 to 10 kilometres above Siberia.
Right below the blast, trees stayed upright but were stripped bare.
A Tunguska-size airburst occurred over a major city.
It would not all happen at once.

paragraphs.text: A 50-metre rock flattened 2,150 square kilometres of forest.
Start with the assumption. Widespread structural damage across an area the size of a metropolis, without any crater.
That is the first effect — but not the biggest. Assume a Tunguska-size airburst occurred over a major city.

The second-order effect is stranger. A 50-metre rock flattened 2,150 square kilometres of forest. It exploded in mid-air, leaving no crater. The blast came 5 to 10 kilometres above Siberia. Estimates put its energy at 3 to 30 megatons. Over a city, windows and roofs would fail across that whole area. Right below the blast, trees stayed upright but were stripped bare. So the danger isn't the impact. It's the shockwave from above. The event is attributed to a meteor air burst, the atmospheric explosion of a stony asteroid about 50–60 m (160–200 ft) wide. Occurring over an area of 2,150 km2 (830 sq mi) in the sparsely populated East Siberian taiga, the explosion felled a significant amount of trees. The object is thought to have exploded at an altitude of 5–10 km (3–6 mi) rather than hitting the Earth's surface, leaving no impact crater. Estimates of its energy have ranged from 3–30 megatons of TNT (13–126 PJ). Investigators found a zone, roughly 8 km (5.0 mi) across, where the trees were scorched and devoid of branches, but still standing upright. A stony asteroid that explodes in the air releases its energy as a shockwave rather than a crater. A Tunguska-size airburst occurred over a major city.
And here is where science stops being certain. The governing physics: a stony asteroid that explodes in the air releases its energy as a shockwave rather than a crater.
So what is the answer? The exact timeline depends on how the impossible change happens; the order of effects is what established physics constrains.

miniNarrative: The growth of the modern industry from the late 18th century onward led to massive urbanization and the rise of new great cities, first in Europe and then in other regions, as new opportunities brought huge numbers of migrants from rural communities into urban areas.
England led the way as London became the capital of a world empire and cities across the country grew in locations strategic for manufacturing.
In the United States from 1860 to 1910, the introduction of railroads reduced transportation costs, and large manufacturing centers began to emerge, fueling migration from rural to city areas.

Some industrialized cities were confronted with health challenges associated with overcrowding, occupational hazards of industry, contaminated water and air, poor sanitation, and communicable diseases such as typhoid and cholera.
shorts.payoff: Some companies are building brand-new master-planned cities from scratch on greenfield sites.
